ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.31; Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 114.1-114.3 (Register of Individuals with Significant Control, as added by SA 2019, c 3); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 21.1-21.4 if a federal wrapper entity is used; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 45; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), SC 2017, c 21; FINTRAC rules on client identification, politically exposed persons (PEPs), and beneficial ownership.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (the ISC register is kept by the corporation internally; Alberta and federal registries are not fully public UBO portals; inspection is limited to shareholders and creditors; FINTRAC, CRA, CBSA and law enforcement may compel production; nominee-friendly structures are not permitted to conceal UBOs)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of valid passport of each director and any individual holding 25% or more of shares
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the country of nationality, attested by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada acceded effective 2024-01-11; consular legalization required if origin state is not an Apostille Party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of any corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or chamber of commerce of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the shareholder-state competent authority; consular legalization if the state is not an Apostille Party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized declaration of source of wealth and source of funds for the incorporation capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the incorporator's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the incorporator/UBO's business reputation and trade history (required for documentary LC onboarding)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the incorporator or beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or authenticated banker's attestation with SWIFT reference

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English or French translation of any foreign-language corporate, passport, or bank documents, with translator's affidavit and notarization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing screening against: (1) Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; (2) FINTRAC foreign PEP categories (head of state, senior politicians, senior public officials, judiciary, military, SOE executives and their family members/close associates) requiring enhanced due diligence; (3) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (4) Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky) designated persons; (5) OFAC SDN list for all USD-denominated SWIFT wires and documentary letters of credit; (6) INTERPOL Red Notices for UBO debarment checks. Screening must be performed at onboarding, at each trade finance facility renewal, and immediately upon any sanctions list update; the compliance file must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (administered by the Ministry of Service Alberta and filed through authorized registry agents); NUANS automated name search for Alberta Business Corporations Act entities; federal fallback: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) at ised-isde.canada.ca.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate name must be expressed in English or French using Roman alphabet characters; non-Roman scripts must be transliterated into English or French. The name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element (e.g., 'Alpine Valley Specialty Green Coffee Beans Inc.'). The proposed name must not be confusingly similar to any existing, reserved, or recognized name in the NUANS database per section 10 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act and associated name regulations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Loan or Finance (unless licensed under financial institutions legislation)
Cooperative (unless formed under the Co-operatives Act)
Terms implying federal or provincial government patronage, armed forces, or the Crown
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the NUANS search or Alberta Corporate Registry rejects the proposed name: (1) the applicant may submit a formal written reconsideration request to the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days, attaching corrected distinctive elements and written consents from existing name holders; (2) alternatively, the applicant may reserve a revised name by filing a fresh NUANS search and new reservation fee; (3) where the rejection is erroneous or arbitrary, judicial review may be sought from the Court of King's Bench of Alberta; (4) for a federal wraparound entity, a request for Director's review under the CBCA may be filed within 30 days, followed by a new NUANS reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only as a physical street address in Alberta (no P.O. Box) that is staffed during normal business hours for service of legal documents under section 100 of the ABCA. Virtual or serviced offices are generally accepted by the corporate registry, but trade finance banks, customs brokers, and marine cargo underwriters for containerized green coffee imports will typically require a substantive operational address, storage or warehouse arrangement, or principal place of business at the port of entry (e.g., the Pacific gateway). A purely virtual office profile may trigger enhanced due diligence measures and delay documentary credit or standby LC facility issuance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (~10-15% probability per fiscal year of active operation). CRA may conduct GST/HST or income tax verification visits; CBSA may audit importer records for tariff classification of green Arabica coffee (HS 0901.11); municipal business licensing may require proof of physical presence; FINTRAC does not directly inspect unregulated importers, but the sponsoring financial institution will perform annual KYC/KYB reviews and may request evidence of commercial substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / authorized registry agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Alberta Business Corporations Act incorporation filing (Articles of Incorporation, standard service)
Notarization and Apostille bundle (passport, bank reference, source of wealth/UBO declaration, 3-document set)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public + Government of Alberta / Global Affairs Canada
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff plus notarial fee; prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified English/French translation of foreign-language supporting documents (per set, if required)
Legal due diligence, UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions screening, and corporate structure advice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (approx. 1.5-2.0 hours at CAD 350-450/hour)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Minute book, corporate seal, share certificates, and statutory records
CRA Business Number and GST/HST account registration (no government fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory no-fee; optional outsourced service fee approx. USD 75 if delegated

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account and documentary LC compliance onboarding kit (first financial institution)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; many institutions charge zero for standard onboarding

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended, particularly ss 10 (incorporation), 12 (articles), 13 (contents of articles), 20-24 (corporate name), 100 (registered office), 103 (directors) and 123 (officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, a division of Service Alberta / Corporate Registry eFiling portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) together with the Initial Notice of Directors and Notice of Registered Office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under Alberta law; a provincial business corporation may be incorporated with a nominal issued share capital of one common share (CAD 1.00). No escrow or paid-up capital deposit account is required by the incorporation procedure.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers to the Articles of Incorporation are hereby allotted 1,000 Common Shares of the Corporation at a subscription price of CAD 1.00 per share, and such subscription is accepted, payment to be made in full to the treasury upon call; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation in Alberta be and is hereby fixed and adopted as [street address, city, province, postal code], and that such office be deemed the head office for service and statutory purposes; RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed President, [Name] Secretary-Treasurer, and [Name] Director, each to serve until replaced or re-elected; RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to open the Corporation's bank account and to sign all banking, taxation, and filing instruments as may be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation corporate name clearance and NUANS search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via an accredited NUANS search house or authorized Service Alberta registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name request to a registered NUANS provider; review the preliminary search for conflicts with existing Alberta, federal, or extra-provincial corporate names; if a confusingly similar name is identified, amend the proposed name or submit a further name request before filing the Articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report reveals a conflicting or confusingly similar name, revise and resubmit the name request; no refund applies once the official name search is requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) in prescribed form, including the authorized share structure (e.g. 1,000 common shares without par value), first directors, registered office address, and incorporator signature. Notarization is not required in Alberta; final execution is by signature of each incorporator and, where applicable, consent of each initial director.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (or director acknowledgment)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry returns a deficiency notice (e.g. missing share class details, incomplete address), correct the articles and re-execute; submit a revised Form 1 with the deficiency letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing, name approval, and payment of incorporation fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed Articles of Incorporation, pay the prescribed filing fee (current CAD 400, approximately USD 300), and submit for name approval and statutory review. The eFiling portal validates the proposed name against the provincial corporate register before issuance of the certificate.
required_dossiers: Final signed Articles of Incorporation in electronic form
Payment instrument or online payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected due to name conflict, incomplete fields, or non-compliant share conditions, correct the deficiencies and resubmit; expedited 2-business-day service is available upon payment of an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and corporate minute book setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, the Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation with a unique Alberta Corporation Number. The incorporator or initial directors must then establish the corporate minute book, including by-laws, share register, directors register, officers register, and seal register; record the issue of common shares.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed, request a status confirmation from Corporate Registry; if any statutory notice was misrecorded, file the appropriate amendment or notice of correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation governance, tax registrations, and federal registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; Alberta Tax and Revenue; Federal Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting of directors to adopt the formation resolutions, approve the issue of shares, adopt the registered office, and appoint officers. File CRA Request for a Business Number (RC1 or online) to obtain a federal BN and any required GST/HST, import/export, or payroll accounts. Alberta corporate income tax registration is generally automatic with the federal registration; confirm any provincial matter with Alberta Tax and Revenue.
required_dossiers: First board resolution appointing officers and confirming share subscription
Directors' full names, residential addresses, and dates of birth
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA BN application is delayed, obtain an acknowledgment and follow up; do not invoice before the BN is confirmed where tax registration is required; correct any officer information by filing a Notice of Change with the Registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial or manufacturing licensing authority is triggered for wholesale distribution of green coffee beans; municipal development and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety authorities apply if a physical warehouse or distribution facility is established.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (for physical premises) and, if importing green coffee beans, a federal Safe Food for Canadians Act import licence under the Canadian Food Inspection Agency; no Alberta provincial industrial operating permit is required for non-manufacturing wholesale distribution.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not triggered — no extraction, manufacturing, or hazardous effluent-generating activity; an EIA registration is only required under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act if a new warehouse or handling facility triggers a permit threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If warehousing or transloading of green coffee beans occurs, no wastewater discharge beyond standard municipal sewer use is expected; comply with applicable municipal sewer by-laws, VOC or dust emission thresholds are not anticipated, and coffee bean storage must follow good housekeeping and spill containment practices in accordance with the Alberta Fire Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code for any storage or distribution facility; carry out structural load inspections and building code compliance for storage racking and mezzanine floors; comply with the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code, including injury prevention, first aid, load anchoring, and workplace safety clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the CRA Business Registration Online service and My Business Account portal. Alberta corporate registrations and provincial filings are administered separately by Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized registry agent or applicable Alberta online services. Alberta has no general provincial sales tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Canadian corporation generally obtains a nine-digit Business Number (BN) from the CRA upon incorporation or by registering through CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1. The corporation must then open the applicable CRA program accounts, including GST/HST, payroll, import-export, and corporation income tax accounts as required. A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada must obtain a BN and register for applicable CRA program accounts using the CRA non-resident registration process or Form RC1. GST/HST registration is required when the corporation is not a small supplier or voluntarily elects registration. Commercial importers and exporters must obtain an import-export program account and use the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) CARM Client Portal for commercial customs transactions. An Alberta corporation or extra-provincial corporation must also complete applicable Alberta Corporate Registry registration. Registration does not itself establish Canadian tax residence; residence depends principally on incorporation and central management and control, subject to applicable treaty rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian corporations are generally subject to entity-level federal and provincial corporate income tax. Canada does not have a United States-style check-the-box election for ordinary corporations. Available elections are transaction- or status-specific, including elections concerning capital dividends, eligible dividends, tax-deferred transfers under section 85 of the Income Tax Act, amalgamations, wind-ups, partnerships, and certain reorganizations. A corporation may qualify for the small business deduction if statutory conditions are met, including Canadian-controlled private corporation requirements where applicable. Alberta corporate tax status is coordinated through the CRA corporate tax filing system; there is no general Alberta pass-through election for a corporation. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are addressed through specific Canadian anti-avoidance, foreign affiliate, thin-capitalization, transfer-pricing, and hybrid arrangement rules rather than a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), a federal value-added tax administered by the CRA. Alberta does not impose a general provincial sales tax. Certain supplies may also be subject to separate federal excise, customs, or provincial regulatory charges.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, generally measured over the relevant preceding four consecutive calendar quarters or in a single calendar quarter, is the small-supplier threshold for most businesses. Taxable supplies made in Canada, including zero-rated supplies, are generally relevant to the threshold; supplies that are exempt and certain specified supplies are excluded. A person exceeding the threshold must register and begin charging GST under the applicable effective-date rules. Voluntary registration is permitted in many cases before the threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general nationwide real-time GST invoice-clearance, mandatory government e-invoicing, or digital tax-stamping regime for ordinary business-to-business transactions. A GST registrant must issue documentation containing prescribed information when required, maintain reliable electronic or paper books and records, and retain records for the statutory retention period, generally six years from the end of the relevant year. CRA electronic filing and payment obligations may apply by taxpayer type and filing period. Customs declarations for commercial imports and exports are processed through CBSA systems, including the CARM Client Portal; this is a customs reporting requirement, not a general GST invoice-clearance mandate. Electronic invoices and accounting records must be capable of substantiating tax charged, input tax credits, export treatment, and audit trails.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada may generally be zero-rated for GST where the statutory export conditions are satisfied, including delivery or export outside Canada in accordance with the Excise Tax Act and supporting evidence that the goods left Canada. Green coffee beans imported into Canada and subsequently exported may qualify for zero-rating on the Canadian export supply if the exporter retains evidence of export and the supply otherwise meets the statutory requirements. GST paid on qualifying imports and Canadian business inputs may generally be recovered through input tax credits, subject to registration, documentary, timing, and attribution rules. Services supplied to non-residents may be zero-rated only where the specific exported-service rules apply; the status of the customer alone is insufficient, and exclusions apply for services connected with Canadian real property, tangible personal property, litigation, and certain services performed in Canada. Exporters must not charge GST on a qualifying zero-rated export but must retain objective evidence linking the transaction, goods, purchaser, carrier, export declaration, and destination outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA commercial export declaration or applicable Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) record, where export reporting is required
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, purchaser, goods, value, origin, destination, and terms of sale
Bill of lading, airway bill, carrier manifest, or equivalent transport document
Packing list and container or shipment identification records
Customs release, import-entry, or delivery evidence in the destination country where available
Proof of delivery or other objective evidence confirming that the goods left Canada
Purchase and sales contracts, purchase orders, documentary letter of credit records, and payment records where relevant
GST import documentation, including CBSA accounting records and proof of GST paid, when claiming related input tax credits

Inward remittance certificate: not generally required under Canadian GST law; bank records or other payment evidence should nevertheless be retained where relevant to commercial, transfer-pricing, anti-money-laundering, or audit substantiation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds and no general requirement to obtain an inward remittance certificate to support GST zero-rating. CRA and CBSA may audit export documentation, supply terms, transportation evidence, customs declarations, inventory records, payment flows, related-party pricing, and the identity and destination of the purchaser. If zero-rating is denied, GST may be assessed retroactively, together with applicable arrears interest and penalties. Incorrectly claimed input tax credits or refunds may be reassessed with interest and penalties. A gross-negligence penalty may generally equal 50% of the overstated tax benefit or understated net tax, while other statutory penalties may apply for late filing, late payment, false statements, repeated failures, or failure to maintain records. Deliberate tax fraud or false customs declarations may result in prosecution, fines, imprisonment, seizure, administrative monetary penalties, customs reassessment, loss of refund entitlement, and recovery of improperly obtained refunds. Export evidence must be retained for CRA audit and limitation-period purposes, generally at least six years, subject to extended periods for non-compliance, objection, appeal, or statutory exception.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange-control authority; the foreign-exchange administration is the shared remit of the Department of Finance Canada, the Bank of Canada (currency issuance and monetary policy), and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for cross-border movement reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Prudential supervision of the domestic commercial banks rests with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), and trade data flows through the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) under the Customs Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction with full current-account and capital-account convertibility. There is no exchange-control licensing, no import-cover requirement, no advance-payment restriction, and no repatriation moratorium affecting green-coffee import payments, profit remittances, or shareholder dividends. The only residual frictions are fiscal rather than FX-regulatory: (i) Part XIII withholding tax at the statutory 25% on dividends and royalties and, subject to the arm's-length-interest exemption, interest paid to non-residents, generally treaty-reduced to 5% to 15%; (ii) Part XIV branch-profit tax, which is relevant only if the specialty-coffee business were conducted through a non-resident branch rather than through the incorporated CA_CORP; and (iii) the thin-capitalization and back-to-back debt rules in Income Tax Act subsections 18(4) to 18(6), 90(6) to 90(13), and 212(3.1), which may recharacterize excessive non-resident shareholder debt as equity and disallow interest. In practice, a federally incorporated or Alberta-registered Business Corporation faces no convertibility obstacle: dividends may be paid at any frequency, subject to corporate solvency rules, the CRA T2 return, the Form T106 non-arm's-length reporting where applicable, and the Form NR4 withholding summary.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable to Canada. Since the repeal of the Foreign Exchange Control Act in 1951, Canada imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no central-bank escrow or surrender obligation on export receipts; the Canadian dollar is freely floating and fully convertible. For the inbound-import model in this dossier, the relevant obligations are: (i) electronic import declaration using HS code 0901.11 (green coffee, not roasted, not decaffeinated) filed through the CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) platform; (ii) retention of all transactional books and records for six years under section 230 of the Income Tax Act; and (iii) FINTRAC reporting of any cross-border electronic funds transfer, or sequential series of transfers, that aggregates CAD 10,000 or more within a 24-hour period. Any origin-country export-proceeds surrender obligation is a matter of the supplier's local FX regime and is contractually neutralized through the confirmed documentary letter of credit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Business Corporations Act, s. 115)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs an additional fee; the corporation cannot obtain a Certificate of Compliance; continued failure for 3 or more years may result in administrative strike-off/dissolution by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Alberta corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for Canada and Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after tax year-end; June 30 for a December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; failure to report or false statements may trigger gross negligence penalties and prosecutorial action under the Income Tax Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a non-distributing Alberta corporation when all shareholders unanimously waive the appointment of an auditor; an independent audit is compulsory for distributing corporations or if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares request one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) under Canadian GAAP for private corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not require a separate UBO annual filing; however, the corporation must maintain a register of individuals with significant control and update it within 15 days of any shareholding transfer or significant control change. Failing to maintain the register or providing false entries carries fines and imprisonment under the Business Corporations Act.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined general corporate active business rate (15% federal general rate + 8% Alberta general rate); Canadian-controlled private corporations pay 11.0% combined (9% federal + 2% Alberta) on the first CA$500,000 of active business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays apply to specialty green coffee bean trading. Available incentives include the refundable SR&ED investment tax credit (35% for qualifying CCPCs, 15% for non-CCPCs), the Alberta Innovation Employment Grant (20% of eligible R&D wages, capped at CA$60,000 per employee per year), and accelerated capital cost allowance for qualifying distribution and technology assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the Canada Revenue Agency's Corporations Internet Filing system using CRA-certified tax preparation software; provincial corporate tax for Alberta is integrated into the T2 return under the federal-provincial corporate tax collection agreement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (12 fiscal months; a short first-year return is permitted for a newly incorporated entity)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return and any balance of tax due must be filed no later than the last day of the sixth month following the corporation's fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the due date is June 30 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, CRA Business Number (BN), corporation program account 'RC0001', registered office in Alberta, incorporation jurisdiction, fiscal year-end, and residency classification checkboxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Canadian resident agent's full address; if the corporation is incorporated federally or in Alberta and managed and controlled from abroad, declare deemed-residency status under ITA s.250 and attach the relevant treaty tie-breaker information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from sales of specialty green coffee beans, container resale, freight recoveries, and ancillary import services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation earning income through a permanent establishment in Alberta reports only Canada-source revenue attributable to that PE; a resident corporation reports worldwide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after cost of goods sold, warehousing, logistics, customs brokerage, financing costs, capital cost allowance, and deductible reserve claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses incurred to earn Canadian income; all cross-border purchase and intercompany allocations must be supported by contemporaneous arm's length documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed federal and Alberta corporate tax after applying the small business deduction, general rate reduction, provincial corporate tax credits, and investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-controlled corporations cannot claim the small business deduction; the general combined rate of 23% applies. The Alberta component is allocated under the Alberta permanent establishment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims the CCPC small business deduction on the first CA$500,000 of active business income, subject to investment income and passive income clawback thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not available to a corporation not controlled by Canadian residents; mark the CCPC ownership declaration only when statutory Canadian control tests are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month, up to 12 months (maximum 17%); repeat failures double the penalty. Delinquent amounts bear prescribed CRA daily compound interest. Failure to file T106/NR4/T5 information returns carries additional per-day penalties and may result in arbitrary assessment and compliance enforcement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on dividends paid to a non-resident shareholder; reduced to 5% under the Canada–US Treaty for a corporate beneficial owner holding at least 10% of voting shares, and to 15% for portfolio shareholders; other Canadian income tax treaties commonly provide rates from 5% to 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Canadian payor must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and, where required, a completed certification form such as CRA Form NR301, from the non-resident beneficial owner before applying the reduced treaty rate. If documentation is incomplete, the payor must withhold the full 25% and the non-resident may apply to the CRA for a refund under Form NR301 with the TRC and treaty article citation. The payor reports all distributions on Form NR4 and the NR4 Summary.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 25% for royalties and 25% for non-arm's length interest; arm's length interest paid to a non-resident lender is generally exempt under ITA s.212(1)(b)(vii). Treaty rates vary by DTA; under the Canada–US Convention royalties are generally limited to 10% and interest to 10%–15%, subject to domestic arm's length exemptions and anti-deferral rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CA$1,000,000 in aggregate annual non-arm's length cross-border transactions, triggering the T106 information return and contemporaneous Local File/Master File documentation. Multinational groups with consolidated annual group revenue above CA$750,000,000 must also file a Country-by-Country Report with the CRA.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no separate Economic Substance Regulation regime, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR), statutory PE rules (ITA s.253), and substance-over-form doctrine require genuine board oversight, employees, inventory risk, title passage, and strategic decision-making in Alberta. A letter-box coffee importer may be deemed resident abroad or denied treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating specialty green coffee revenue, falsifying customs and corporate invoices, destroying books and records, or parking Canadian profits in an offshore shell without genuine business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.239 prosecution: fine of 50%–200% of the tax sought to be evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment, plus gross negligence civil penalties of 50% of the understated tax, interest, and revocation of compliance status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign or direct false returns are jointly and severally liable for restitution of taxes and penalties; criminal conviction exposes individuals to incarceration, global asset freeze, and for non-Canadian directors, IRPA inadmissibility and removal from Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unremitted Withholding Taxes (Part XIII, Payroll, GST/HST)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, or wages to non-residents or employees without deducting and remitting the required Part XIII, payroll source deductions, or GST/HST.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may assess the corporation for the full unremitted amount, compound daily prescribed interest, late penalties of up to 10% of the unremitted amount, and information-return penalties; repeated behaviour triggers criminal referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable under ITA s.227.1 and Excise Tax Act s.323 for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST; CRA may seize personal assets, issue director's assessment, and prohibit cross-border travel for senior officers while enforcement is outstanding.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing green coffee from a related non-resident trader at inflated prices, overpaying royalties or management fees to a tax-haven affiliate, or maintaining an artificial distribution route with no operational substance in Alberta.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA audit adjustments to reassess taxable income at arm's length, 10% transfer pricing penalty under ITA s.247(3) on net adjustments, denial of treaty relief, and GAAR penalties of up to 50% of the tax benefit; failure to file T106 adds separate penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not shielded by the corporate veil where they knowingly sign false transfer pricing filings or cause GAAR avoidance transactions; personal exposure includes civil restitution of avoided taxes, fines for counselling false statements, and imprisonment for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing large coffee-import payments without verifying beneficial ownership, failing to record large cash transactions or suspicious transactions, using untraceable shell entities to settle documentary letters of credit, or making false OFSI/FINTRAC declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, administrative monetary penalties of up to CA$1,000,000 per violation; Criminal Code money-laundering offences carry imprisonment up to 10 years and unlimited fines, with proceeds subject to civil forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior officers who authorize AML breaches are personally criminally liable; convictions result in imprisonment, confiscation of personal and corporate assets, travel bans pending extradition or sentencing, and permanent inadmissibility for non-residents.
